correctness.rationale: For distinct singleton partial injections any nonempty composite of both orders gives different maps; commuting therefore requires that neither ordered composite is nonempty. Aggregate source and target supports of a face are disjoint, not necessarily singleton or pairwise different within each support. An independent all-n proof uses simplex weights lambda_ij: their row and column marginals p,q have disjoint supports, and x=p-q has coordinate sum zero and ℓ1 norm 2. Conversely x returns the weights lambda_ij=x_i^+ x_j^- because each sign part sums to 1. For a starting simplex point, interpolation to the weights returned by its marginals stays within the simplex of all arcs between its original two supports, and fixes the section pointwise. This is equivariant under label permutations and transposition of indices. On the resulting sphere in the sum-zero hyperplane the determinant of a coordinate permutation is its sign, and the determinant of inversion is (-1)^(n-1). This proves the integral orientation-lattice claim, including reduced H0 at n=2. The frozen mod-two and integral trace computations are finite checks, not the integral theorem.
